## Overview

My PhD research explores **mycosanitation** — using filamentous fungi to make
sanitation safer and more circular. I investigate how fungi can reduce pathogens
in faecal sludge and transform waste materials into valuable resources, an
emerging and largely unexplored field at the interface of mycology and global
health engineering.

Before my PhD I worked on fungi from a different angle: biocontrol and
mycopesticides in agriculture at Agroscope, and the molecular biology of fungal
plant pathogens during my studies at ETH Zürich.

## Research interests

- **Mycosanitation** — filamentous fungi for treating faecal sludge and reducing
  pathogens
- **Waste-to-resource** — transforming waste materials into valuable products
  through fungal processes
- **Fungal biocontrol & mycopesticides** — optimising fungi for pest and
  pathogen management
- **Fungal plant pathogens** — regulation and evolution of virulence
- **Pathogen viability methods** — helminth-egg (*Ascaris*) viability assays and
  microscopy tooling
